claim: Atomic lifecycle commits: every commit recording an authoring-lifecycle transition records exactly one transition of one artifact - one thread captured or updated, one focus brief opened, updated, or graduated, one focus's manifest rows minted. A commit conjoining separable lifecycle events is a mis-authored bundle, split at commit time: the belief atomicity doctrine transposed from nodes to commits. Atomic means one event, not one file - a brief together with the index and manifest updates it forces is one event. Typed trailers (Thread:, Focus:, Belief:) therefore map one-to-one onto commits, so a trailer grep returns exactly one artifact's history.

evidence.detail: Adopted by operator decision in the 2026-07-02 authoring-pipeline session after reviewing an atomic-commits policy (every completed task its own commit, message tracing to the planning document). The review validated the existing one-commit-per-lifecycle-event lean and sharpened it: the first round trip supplied two motivating counterexamples, d7e40cb bundling four Focus: events and ae0e63f bundling two focuses' mints. The atomicity discipline is adopted alone: CB keeps its typed, CI-enforced trailers over prose-in-message linkage, and a ROADMAP/SUMMARY document apparatus is explicitly not adopted (the SUMMARY-file shape is the cb:b386 cached-digest antipattern). The landing sequence of this belief is the first compliant instance: thread update (c2b342c), brief update (the cited commit), and this mint as three per-focus commits. Preflight 2026-07-02: clean - 0 contract, 0 schema, 24 neutral; the b538 concurrent-sweep action-item reviewed as complementary (atomic commits narrow the sweep surface but do not discharge it).
